patterns: True LDC-built or LDC-owned pipe for data centers is rare in what I could find; most new pipe is built by midstream or intrastate transmission companies and is transmission scale. The clearest LDC cases are in Ohio (a local gas cooperative and Hope Utilities' subsidiary), where regulators do not require pre-approval for single-customer intrastate lines. Memphis shows the other form, a small tap off an existing LDC main. No source gave a length for any LDC-built line, so row counts are possible but km are not. Utility commission special contracts exist (Atmos says data centers need special contracts with customer-paid system fortification) but the dockets rarely surface in web search.
not_found: No data-center-specific LDC pipe found for NIPSCO (sources cover GenCo power plants only), Columbia Gas of Ohio (its 4.2-mile line served Intel, not a data center), Spire, CenterPoint, Southwest Gas, Black Hills, Dominion or Virginia Natural Gas, Piedmont, Xcel, or Georgia and Arizona LDCs (Arizona and Entergy Louisiana lines are Energy Transfer transmission or laterals, not LDC). Washington Gas (AltaGas) reported two small data center gas supply deals in Maryland and Virginia, but I did not open the source. DatacenterDynamics, S&P Global and MLGW PDF pages were blocked or errored so those details are unverified. I did not search state commission dockets directly.
